title: Lecture 13 — arithmetic circuits, ALU and flags
summary: Derive adders, control subtraction and interpret ALU status flags without confusing carry with signed overflow.
body:
Begin with the half-adder and full-adder truth tables, then compose a multibit arithmetic circuit. Trace carries in the direction they actually propagate. Compare ripple, lookahead and carry-select designs by their dependency paths and hardware cost.

Reuse the adder for subtraction, then connect arithmetic and logic blocks to an ALU result selector. Interpret N, Z, C and V separately, and use deliberately contrasting signed and unsigned examples to test the distinction. End by using subtraction to compare operands under the declared representation.
